summary: Implement an idempotent shutdown lifecycle with admission fencing, active-work accounting, bounded drain, cleanup ordering, and clean-versus-forced evidence.
triggers: A service or worker must stop accepting work and drain tracked activity.
Shutdown readiness, duplicate signals, cleanup, or timeout behavior needs review.
A termination receipt must distinguish clean completion from forced exit.
antiTriggers: Stop a production process without the required operational scope.
Choose a deadline without evidence of the host grace window.
Assume one listener close drains every transport or worker.

provenance.note: Method source read in full and independently rewritten for portable product use; the historical file remains unchanged.
Lifecycle operations, failure cases, and termination semantics informed the rewrite; no source prose was copied.
Ownership and evidence boundaries were consulted; this is instruction-reviewed, not a runtime qualification.
